ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=-x$ intersects with the line $y=x+b$ at point A. If the ordinate of point A is 1, what is the solution set of the inequality $x+b<-x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the line $y=-x$ intersects with the line $y=x+b$ at point A, and the ordinate of point A is 1,\\
$\therefore$ $-x=1$,\\
Solving this, we get $x=-1$,\\
which means the abscissa of point A is $-1$,\\
$\therefore$ the solution set of the inequality $x+b<-x$ is $\boxed{x<-1}$.
